title: Counting failed requests
prompt: Someone wanted the number of failed requests (status 400 or more) and wrote this. What does it actually print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
failed = api_requests.rdd.map(lambda r: r["status_code"] >= 400)
print(failed.count())
print(failed.take(3))
hints: Which RDD transformation keeps or drops items, and which one turns each item into something else?
`map` always gives back one item for every item it starts with.
Each item is now whatever the comparison returned. Check the first three status codes.
explanation: `map` doesn't drop anything: it turns each of the 12 requests into `True` or `False`, so `count()` is 12. The first three requests all succeeded, so their items are `False`. To keep only the failed ones, use `filter` with the same function; that gives 2.
